dogecoin.text: @ceresbzns Stuff like bitcoin, xrp, litecoin, dogecoin etc
@TheStalwart Another difference for new folks is that Dogecoin is quite conservative. The code is the same year in year out. But bitcoin is less conservative – its code is always being updated.

@MacRoweNick I agree. The inflation tax is a very non-transparent way of paying for electricity. If users actually felt the costs of running schemes like bitcoin or dogecoin via 100% transaction fees, they wouldn't be as eager to sign up.
@BTCmePLZ I mean, we agree that most of what occurs on Dogecoin is pure speculation, right?

@proofofwoof @FedericoTenga @hasufl @lawrencehwhite1 @iang_fc Agreed. The entire schedule of Dogecoin issuance is common knowledge, so the "sell pressure" from the 10,000 Dogecoins created every minute is already factored into Doge's price.

@samkazemian @hasufl @lawrencehwhite1 @iang_fc Sure, Doge may have aesthetic properties, too. But it still uses as much electricity as Vermont. As I said, I suspect this is because Dogecoin owners -- whether they be gamblers or aesthetes -- don't internalize Doge's huge costs because of the mining subsidy.
